solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Stress Musk’s content to follow international court (5)

indicatorNotes.content: a word's content is what sits inside its outer letters
indicatorNotes.to follow: the US comes after the ICT

annotation.surface: A complaint that Elon Musk's posts are now trailing an international court case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as social-media posts; here it means the letters inside MUSK. An ictus is the stress on a syllable in verse.
annotation.definitionFit: In prosody the ictus is the stress or beat falling on a syllable.

entries.clue: Causes of anxiety including money for everyone (6)

blocks.note: inc. is the abbreviation for including

annotation.surface: A worry that a universal cash handout will itself cause anxiety.
annotation.walkthrough: UBI, universal basic income, is a proposed payment to every citizen. Incubi are nightmare demons, so figuratively things that weigh on the mind.
annotation.definitionFit: An incubus is an oppressive burden or nightmare, so incubi are causes of anxiety.

entries.clue: No longer going potty? (6-7)

blocks.note: the surface hears 'no longer going mad'; the setter means a child who has stopped using something
not the slang for crazy but the child's pot, which a trained toddler has left behind for the lavatory

annotation.surface: Someone asking whether a person has regained their sanity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going potty' is British slang for going mad, which is the reading the surface pushes; the literal potty is the child's one.
annotation.definitionFit: Read literally, the clue describes a toddler who has graduated from a potty to the lavatory, which is exactly what training achieves.

entries.clue: Obsessive admirer daughters tolerate (5)

blocks.note: a stan is an obsessive fan, from the Eminem song

annotation.surface: A parent wondering whether the daughters can put up with a superfan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Obsessive admirer' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it only supplies STAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly heard in negatives: someone who can't bear a noise says they can't abide or put up with it.

entries.clue: Back away from angry bluebottle, finally free after the setter’s knocked over lab equipment (10)

indicatorNotes.knocked over: something knocked over is upended, so I'M turns round
indicatorNotes.Back away from: the back letter goes away from CROSS
indicatorNotes.finally: 'finally' points at the last thing in a word, here its closing letter
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' is positional: everything before it in the clue is placed following MI

blocks.note: the setter is = I'M, turned round
bluebottle is old slang for a policeman, from the blue uniform

annotation.surface: Someone backing away from a furious fly, then accidentally knocking over the lab kit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bluebottle' is set up as the fly; in crosswords it is a police officer. 'Back away from' reads as retreating, but it cuts the back letter off 'angry'.
annotation.definitionFit: A microscope is a standard piece of laboratory equipment.

entries.clue: Male dog, having lost lead, regularly peed and wandered aimlessly (7)

indicatorNotes.having lost lead: a word that has lost its lead has lost its first letter
indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so letters are taken at a steady every-other step

annotation.surface: A male dog let off the leash, stopping to pee every few yards as it roams.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lost lead' paints a dog off its leash; it means POOCH losing its leading letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from British informal speech: to mooch around town is to drift about with no purpose.

entries.clue: Established place for nuns on island on lake (12)

blocks.note: Iona, the Hebridean island off Mull

annotation.surface: A convent founded on an island in a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Established' as 'founded', a verb about the convent, but it is the adjective: established ways are conventional ones. IONA is a Scottish island famous for its abbey.
annotation.definitionFit: Conventional practice is the established, accepted way of doing things.

entries.clue: Defeat that hurts touring team, albeit depleted (8)

indicatorNotes.touring: OUCH goes round, as a tour goes round a place
indicatorNotes.depleted: both words are emptied, keeping only their outer letters

blocks.note: what you say when something hurts

annotation.surface: A painful loss for a touring team that was short of players.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depleted' seems to describe a team short of players, but it empties both of the words beside it, keeping only their edges.
annotation.definitionFit: To outmatch an opponent is to prove superior and so defeat them.

entries.clue: Fiscal watchdog started by Conservative, a cold-blooded creature (5)

indicatorNotes.started by: C starts the word, the watchdog follows

blocks.note: the UK's Office for Budget Responsibility

annotation.surface: A political jibe: the budget watchdog, set up by the Tories, is a cold-blooded snake.
annotation.walkthrough: The OBR is Britain's independent fiscal watchdog, created by a Conservative chancellor in 2010, so the surface is a fair political jab. 'A cold-blooded creature' works both as the snake and as the insult.
annotation.definitionFit: A cobra is a snake, and snakes are cold-blooded reptiles.

entries.clue: Append electronic reference work about collection of Old Norse verse (6,4)

blocks.note: to cite is to refer to

annotation.surface: An instruction to add an online reference book about Norse poetry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reference work' pretends to be one thing, an encyclopaedia, but splits in two. Op. is the abbreviation for opus, used in numbering composers' works.
annotation.definitionFit: A factual description: the anthology preserved in the thirteenth-century Icelandic Codex Regius gathers mythological and heroic poems about Odin, Thor and Sigurd.

entries.clue: Was theatrical dame disheartened, as I see it on reflection? (6)

indicatorNotes.disheartened: the heart, the middle letters, is taken out
indicatorNotes.on reflection: a reflection shows things back to front

annotation.surface: Someone asking whether a grand actress had lost her nerve, as it looked to them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Was theatrical dame' reads as one phrase about an actress; the definition stops at 'theatrical'. DE and TO ME, read backwards, give EMOTED.
annotation.definitionFit: To emote is to act with exaggerated feeling, to be theatrical.

entries.clue: Aged parent went off, forgetting name (7)

indicatorNotes.forgetting: what you forget is left out, so the N for name drops from TURNED

blocks.note: TURNED (went off, like milk) without N for name

annotation.surface: An elderly parent who left, forgetting a name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Aged parent' looks like one phrase for an old mum or dad; 'Aged' is the definition alone. 'Went off' means turned sour, as milk does.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs in the past tense: cheese or whisky left for years grows older and ripens.

entries.clue: Newspaper editor, one opening function for actor (9)

indicatorNotes.opening: the paper, editor and one open up TAN and sit inside it

blocks.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

annotation.surface: A newspaper editor opening a charity event for an actor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening function' reads as a gala launch; 'function' is the maths sense, TAN, which RAG, ED and I break open.
annotation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who plays tragic roles.

entries.clue: Nobel laureate and woman cycling north (5)

indicatorNotes.cycling: letters move from the front of the word to the back

blocks.note: LADY with LA moved to the end

annotation.surface: A prizewinner and a woman out on a bike ride heading north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' is set up as riding a bicycle; it means rotating the letters of LADY. Bob Dylan won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the singer-songwriter Bob won the 2016 literature prize from the Swedish Academy.

entries.clue: Current sweetheart removing old underwear introduces villainous character (4,4,6)

indicatorNotes.removing: the O for old is taken out of LOVER
indicatorNotes.introduces: the underwear comes first and introduces the rest

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A current partner who is throwing out the old thermal underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current sweetheart' reads as someone's present partner; 'Current' gives I on its own. Long John Silver is the one-legged pirate of Treasure Island.
annotation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the villain of Stevenson's Treasure Island.

entries.clue: Security organisation with cracking feature film (9)

indicatorNotes.cracking: NATO and W break into CHIN

annotation.surface: A security body with a hit feature film on its hands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cracking feature film' sounds like a rave review, with 'cracking' as British praise; here it means breaking open, and 'feature' is part of a face.
annotation.definitionFit: Chinatown is the 1974 film noir starring Jack Nicholson.

entries.clue: Board pay for party game (5,8)

blocks.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging
to foot the bill is to pay it
a ball is a dance party

annotation.surface: A company board agreeing to pay for a party game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party game' looks like a single phrase; 'party' gives BALL and 'game' is the definition. Table football is foosball.
annotation.definitionFit: Table football is a game played with rods of little footballers.

entries.clue: Extent of study most of the book initiates (7)

indicatorNotes.most of: most of a word is all but a bit of it, here everything except its last letter
indicatorNotes.initiates: to initiate is to begin, so the book's B stands at the start

blocks.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

annotation.surface: How widely a student must read: most of the set text before starting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extent of study' reads as a single phrase about a syllabus; only 'Extent' defines. To read a subject is the British university sense of study it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the width or range of something, as when a critic praises how widely a scholar's knowledge reaches.

entries.clue: Sending forth European delegating authority to missing Democrat (9)

indicatorNotes.to missing: the D for Democrat goes missing

annotation.surface: A European handing power to a Democrat who has gone missing.
annotation.walkthrough: To mandate is to give authority to someone; the D then drops out.
annotation.definitionFit: Emanating means issuing or sending forth, as light emanates from a lamp.

entries.clue: Using the local tongue, river guide enthrals husband (5)

indicatorNotes.enthrals: to enthral once meant to hold in thrall, captive, so REIN keeps H held inside it

annotation.surface: A river guide who charms a husband by speaking the local language.
annotation.walkthrough: 'River guide' sounds like a boatman; 'river' belongs to the definition and 'guide' is REIN. The Rhein is the Rhine in German, the local tongue.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhein is the German name of the Rhine, the river as locals say it.

entries.clue: Son ran this person’s drinking spot — he’ll try to stop thieves (5,9)

blocks.note: to spot something is to detect it
I'VE: this person, the setter, has
surface padding for a pub; the pieces simply run in order

annotation.surface: A son running the setter's local bar, and a note that he will try to stop thieves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drinking spot' reads as a bar, but 'spot' is a verb here, meaning notice, and 'drinking' only dresses the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a plain-clothes guard employed by a shop, whose job is catching shoplifters before they leave.

entries.clue: White wine imbibed by glamorous setter (9)

indicatorNotes.imbibed by: the answer has been swallowed by the words that follow

annotation.surface: A glamorous crossword setter sipping white wine.
annotation.walkthrough: Roussette is a white grape and wine of Savoie; it straddles the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an Alpine appellation from Savoie in eastern France, made from the Altesse grape.

entries.clue: Did meditation, free of concerning wobbles (8)

indicatorNotes.free of: to be free of something is to be rid of it, so ON leaves MEDITATION
indicatorNotes.wobbles: the remaining letters shake into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone who meditated but was still anxious and shaky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Did meditation' reads as a verb and its object; 'Did' alone is the definition, as in 'she did the Queen', meaning impersonated.
annotation.definitionFit: To do someone, as an impressionist does, is to imitate them.

entries.clue: Consecrates roads in Barking (7)

indicatorNotes.Barking: barking means mad, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: A bishop blessing new roads in Barking, a town in east London.
annotation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, and the capital letter makes it a place; in the wordplay it is the slang for mad.
annotation.definitionFit: To ordain is to consecrate someone as a priest.

entries.clue: Briefly look over painter’s note in shock (10)

blocks.note: to scan is to look over quickly

annotation.surface: Glancing at a painter's note and being shocked by it.
annotation.walkthrough: Dalí is the usual crossword painter; his note leaves one scandalised.
annotation.definitionFit: To scandalise is to shock people by offending their sense of propriety.

entries.clue: Something divisive that may put you off your stroke? (5,5)

annotation.definition2: may put you off your stroke?

blocks.note: the political sense: a topic chosen to split the other side

blocks.clueFragment: may put you off your stroke?
blocks.note: the golf sense: a problem with your wedge, a lofted club

annotation.surface: A golfer blaming a fault in the wedge for a bad shot.
annotation.walkthrough: A wedge issue is a political topic used to split an opponent's supporters. The question mark flags the golf reading: a wedge is a club, and an issue with it would spoil your stroke.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: American political slang for a topic that splits a coalition, and literally trouble with a golfer's lofted club.

entries.clue: Appraisal of mixture of olive and tuna pasta, ultimately (10)

indicatorNotes.mixture of: a mixture blends ingredients together, so the fodder's letters are stirred into a new order
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the end letter of pasta counts

annotation.surface: A food critic's verdict on an olive and tuna pasta dish.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a restaurant review, and an appraisal is exactly what a review is.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a judgement of worth, such as a manager's yearly review of staff performance.

entries.clue: Laid into women’s novel lacking in depth (3-11)

indicatorNotes.novel: the letters take a new form

annotation.surface: A critic savaging a women's novel for having shallow characters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' is set up as a book, and it is the anagram instruction. A two-dimensional character is exactly the complaint the surface's critic makes.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: flat shapes have width and height but no third axis, so shallow fictional characters get called this.

entries.clue: Ulterior motive that’s characteristic of Häagen-Dazs? (6,6)

blocks.note: the brand name hides AGENDA: HäAGEN-DAzs

annotation.surface: A suspicion that an ice-cream brand has a secret motive.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a crossword joke: the letters AGENDA are literally hidden inside Häagen-Dazs.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for a concealed purpose, and literally true of the ice-cream brand, whose spelling conceals those six letters.

entries.clue: Declined to leave excellent books about New England (4,2,3)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' in its sense of around: the other pieces wrap round NE like a fence round a field

blocks.note: OT = Old Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: Someone who refused to part with first-rate books on New England.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Declined' looks like 'refused'; it means deteriorated. OT is the Old Testament.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning deteriorated badly, as a neglected garden or a failing business does.

entries.clue: Shape of old Indian city outlined by His Majesty (8)

indicatorNotes.outlined by: HM draws a line round the rest

annotation.surface: The king tracing the outline of an old Indian city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shape of old Indian city' reads as a single phrase about a city's layout; 'Shape' is the definition alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A hexagram is a six-pointed star shape.

entries.clue: Brilliant to get shot of island group (5)

indicatorNotes.to get shot of: to get shot of something is to be rid of it

blocks.note: 'that's genius' is informal British praise for something brilliant
I = island; this is the letter removed

annotation.surface: A cheer at finally being rid of a group of islands.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Island group' looks like one phrase, an archipelago; 'group' is the definition. 'Genius' as an adjective (that's genius!) is British slang for brilliant.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical sense from biology: the rank above species, grouping closely related organisms such as lions and tigers.

entries.clue: Test digital assistant installed by groups of schoolchildren lacking boundaries (4,4)

indicatorNotes.installed by: something installed is fitted inside a place, so ALEXA is set within the other letters
indicatorNotes.lacking boundaries: FORMS loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: FORMS (school classes) without the F and S at its edges

annotation.surface: Schools installing a digital assistant in classrooms to test pupils.
annotation.walkthrough: A form is a school class in Britain. ALEXA sits inside what is left of FORMS.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: an examination answered out loud to an examiner rather than written down, as viva candidates face.

entries.clue: Longed to grab bite for walrus? (8)

indicatorNotes.to grab: PINED grabs NIP and holds it inside

blocks.note: a nip is a small bite

annotation.surface: A walrus longing to take a bite.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark says the walrus is only one example: pinnipeds are the seals, sea lions and walruses.
annotation.definitionFit: A walrus is a pinniped, a fin-footed marine mammal.

entries.clue: Can worker rebuild ropier coffins? (6,7)

indicatorNotes.rebuild: the letters are rebuilt in another order

annotation.surface: Asking whether an undertaker's worker can remake some shoddy coffins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as the verb 'is able to'; it is slang for prison. Ropey is British slang for poor quality.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: American usage calls a jail 'the can', so a warder employed there is someone working in it.

entries.clue: Initially, this grift sat awkwardly (2,5,5)

indicatorNotes.awkwardly: the letters sit awkwardly, out of order

annotation.surface: Someone uneasy about a con from the start.
annotation.walkthrough: A grift is a swindle; the surface says the scam felt wrong from the beginning.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for the opening impression, before closer inspection changes one's view, as in love on a first meeting.

entries.clue: Thoroughly popular Irish parliament hosting drug summit at last (2,6)

indicatorNotes.hosting: DAIL hosts the drug and summit's end inside it
indicatorNotes.at last: 'at last' means at the very end, so only the final letter of summit is used

annotation.surface: The Irish parliament hosting a summit on drugs to popular acclaim.
annotation.walkthrough: The Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament; E and T go inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: An adverbial phrase: covering every particular, as a report examined point by point rather than skimmed.

entries.clue: Congratulations puzzle lieutenant, more than half-cut (8)

indicatorNotes.half-cut: read literally rather than as slang for tipsy: a word cut in half keeps only its first two letters

annotation.surface: Congratulating a lieutenant who is rather drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, and 'more than half-cut' reads as very drunk; it means half of OVER.
annotation.definitionFit: Mazel tov is a Hebrew and Yiddish expression of congratulations.

entries.clue: Either four or six absent from unimportant court proceedings (5)

indicatorNotes.absent from: someone absent from a place is missing from it, so the numeral goes missing from the word

blocks.note: Roman IV (four), or VI (six) — the letters removed

annotation.surface: A trivial court case where four or six people failed to turn up.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is candid that it does not matter which: the IV and VI in TRIVIAL are the same letters, so dropping either leaves TRIAL.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the hearing where a judge or jury examines evidence and decides guilt.

entries.clue: Company called the French heads of inventory and sales for instrument (3,7)

indicatorNotes.heads of: a word's head is its front, so each word supplies its leading letter

blocks.note: the first letters of Inventory and Sales

annotation.surface: A company that phoned French department heads for an instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like business paperwork, but 'heads of' just picks initial letters. A cor anglais is the English horn.
annotation.definitionFit: The cor anglais is a woodwind instrument of the oboe family.

entries.clue: Computer user misused legal authority (7,5)

indicatorNotes.misused: the letters are used wrongly, in the wrong order

annotation.surface: A computer user who has abused legal powers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Misused legal authority' reads as abuse of power, but 'misused' shuffles the first two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the highest tribunal in many countries, whose rulings bind every lower judge.

entries.clue: Streamer perhaps posted car crashes (9)

indicatorNotes.crashes: the letters crash and come out jumbled

annotation.surface: A streamer posting car-crash videos online.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks a podcaster as one kind of streamer, a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A podcaster is one example of someone who streams content online.

entries.clue: Innovative companies stir proud southern founders (10)

indicatorNotes.founders: to founder is to collapse or sink, so the words before it fall apart into a new order

annotation.surface: Pioneering start-ups whose founders are stirring up the proud South.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stir' and 'founders' both look like business talk; 'stir' is fodder and 'founders' is the verb, collapse, that scrambles it.
annotation.definitionFit: Business jargon: start-ups whose new technology upends an established market, as streaming did to video rental.

entries.clue: Sort of backing singers Danny is periodically employing to begin with (2,1,5)

indicatorNotes.periodically: something that recurs periodically comes back at fixed intervals, here every second letter
indicatorNotes.to begin with: 'to begin with' means at the start, so only the opening letter of employing counts
indicatorNotes.employing: the periodic letters employ E at their front

blocks.note: the odd letters of SiNgErS dAnNy Is

annotation.surface: Backing singers who work with Danny now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing singers' reads as one phrase; 'backing' is the reversal and 'singers' is fodder. E comes first, then the reversal flips everything.
annotation.definitionFit: A hedging phrase: both soften a claim, admitting it holds only partly or from one angle.

entries.clue: Continues to be close by university residence (7)

indicatorNotes.by: the pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: a res is a student residence hall

annotation.surface: Staying on near the university halls.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close by' reads as 'near'; 'close' is the noun, the END.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the third person: a tradition that survives for centuries persists and lasts.

entries.clue: Artist’s hit that felt endless (7)

blocks.note: a rap is a sharp hit

annotation.surface: A painter's hit that seemed to go on for ever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Artist's hit' reads as a popular work; 's is just 'is' joining definition to wordplay. 'Endless' strips both ends from 'that' and 'felt'.
annotation.definitionFit: Raphael is the Italian Renaissance painter.

entries.clue: Notice car stop, probed by Republican government (14)

indicatorNotes.probed by: a probe is pushed into something, so R is poked inside STATION

blocks.note: a station is a stop on a line

annotation.surface: A notice about a car stopped by the Republican government.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Car stop' reads as a traffic stop; it is MINI and STATION, with R pushed into STATION.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, especially in American usage: the Biden or Reagan years name the executive branch in power.

entries.clue: Rodent, one biting hard shrub (7)

indicatorNotes.biting: teeth close round what they bite, so the rodent-plus-one wraps round H

annotation.surface: A rodent gnawing on a tough shrub.
annotation.walkthrough: Rhatany is an obscure South American shrub whose root was used in medicine; the wordplay is the way in.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhatany is a South American shrub of the genus Krameria.

entries.clue: Drink mentioned down under rock band picked up (6)

indicatorNotes.picked up: in a down clue, picked up means read from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.under: in a down answer LOW sits below MER
indicatorNotes.mentioned: said out loud, MER-LOW sounds like the wine

blocks.note: R.E.M., the American rock band, reversed
down = low; the French-derived spelling ends in a silent T

annotation.surface: A drink named at a gig by an Australian rock band.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Down under' looks like Australia; 'down' is LOW and 'under' places it below MER. MER-LOW is how the wine is said.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a red grape from Bordeaux, and the wine made from it, poured by the glass in any bar.

entries.clue: Small instrument out of tune (5)

annotation.surface: A little instrument that won't stay in tune.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small instrument' reads as a single thing, a piccolo perhaps; it is S plus HARP.
annotation.definitionFit: A note that is sharp is pitched too high, out of tune.

entries.clue: Second corporation acquiring large shaft (5)

indicatorNotes.acquiring: a firm acquiring another takes it in, so TUM takes L into its middle

blocks.note: corporation is jocular British slang for a pot belly, a tum

annotation.surface: A second company buying a large shaft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company; in old slang it means a big belly, TUM. A stulm is a horizontal mine passage.
annotation.definitionFit: A stulm is an adit or level shaft driven into a mine.

entries.clue: Manages courses in agronomy, partly retired (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer lies in the words
indicatorNotes.partly: only part of the words is used

annotation.surface: A retired farmer who now runs courses in agronomy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Partly retired' reads as semi-retired; it says the letters are a part and run backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: To organise something is to manage it.

entries.clue: Some bemoan a horrible biblical character (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: some of the letters give the answer

annotation.surface: Complaining about a dreadful figure from the Bible.
annotation.walkthrough: Nahor is Abraham's brother (and grandfather) in Genesis, obscure enough that the hidden word is the way in.
annotation.definitionFit: Nahor is a figure in Genesis, brother of Abraham.

entries.clue: Somewhat advanced temperature gun (1,6)

annotation.surface: A gun that is running rather hot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat advanced' reads as a single phrase; 'Somewhat' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A trifle means slightly, somewhat: a trifle tired.

entries.clue: Man in pub recalled treatment for addiction (5)

indicatorNotes.in: a man in a pub is inside it, so HE sits within BAR

annotation.surface: A man in a pub remembering his time in treatment.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a drinker remembering rehab; 'recalled' is really a reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: Short for rehabilitation, the clinic programme that helps people recover from dependence on drink or drugs.

entries.clue: Running event in rural Oman that collapsed (13)

indicatorNotes.collapsed: the letters collapse into a new order

annotation.surface: A desert race in rural Oman that ended with runners collapsing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Collapsed' fits the surface, a runner collapsing in desert heat, and is also the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An ultramarathon is a running race longer than a marathon.

entries.clue: Introduction to guerrilla soldiers with big guns, reportedly capricious with figures (9)

indicatorNotes.Introduction to: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter of guerrilla is used
indicatorNotes.reportedly: what follows is heard, not spelt

annotation.surface: Guerrilla fighters with heavy guns who behave unpredictably.
annotation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery are the British Army's gunners. 'With figures' means illustrated with diagrams.
annotation.definitionFit: Graphical means using graphs or figures.

entries.clue: Just married on visiting cathedral city (6)

indicatorNotes.visiting: RE goes to stay inside ELY

annotation.surface: Newlyweds visiting a cathedral city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just married' reads as newlyweds; 'Just' is the definition. ELY is a small English cathedral city, a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adverbs: 'it was merely a scratch' and 'it was only a scratch' say the same.

entries.clue: Earl bad-tempered, eating mixed nuts every so often in a greedy manner (10)

indicatorNotes.eating: what you eat goes inside you, so SURLY swallows IENT into its middle
indicatorNotes.every so often: 'every so often' means at intervals, so letters are picked at a regular every-other step

annotation.surface: A grumpy earl gobbling a bowl of mixed nuts now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' looks like an anagram instruction but is fodder, from which alternate letters are taken.
annotation.definitionFit: Esurient means hungry or greedy, so esuriently means greedily.

entries.clue: Bordering on raucous, entering bar for pop (5)

indicatorNotes.Bordering on: the borders are the outer letters
indicatorNotes.entering: someone entering a room goes inside it, so RS goes inside BUT
